import unittest
from unittest.mock import Mock
from fetcher import fetch

class TestFetcher(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        # Set up a mock client object that mimics an HTTP client with a get method
        self.mock_client = Mock()
        self.mock_url = "http://test.com/api"

    def test_fetch_with_timeout(self):
        # Mock the client.get to simulate a successful response
        mock_response = Mock()
        mock_response.status_code = 200
        mock_response.text = "Test Data"
        self.mock_client.get.return_value = mock_response

        # Call the function under test
        result = fetch(self.mock_client, self.mock_url)

        # Assertions
        # 1. Check if client.get was called with the correct arguments, including timeout=30
        self.mock_client.get.assert_called_once_with(self.mock_url, timeout=30)
        # 2. Check if the return value is correct
        self.assertEqual(result, mock_response)

    def test_fetch_propagation_of_exception(self):
        # Mock the client.get to raise an exception
        expected_exception = Exception("Connection Timed Out")
        self.mock_client.get.side_effect = expected_exception

        # Assert that calling fetch raises the expected exception
        with self.assertRaises(Exception) as context:
            fetch(self.mock_client, self.mock_url)

        self.assertEqual(str(context.exception), "Connection Timed Out")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
